title: Recursive shelves: Proof strip
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Divide-and-conquer recursion. Return the whole list.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `sectionSums`. Start with the whole `readings` list as a section. Record the sum of that section. If it has more than one number, split it into a left half and a right half. Use the same steps on the left half first, then on the right half. When a section has an odd length, the left half has one fewer number. A section with one number is not split. Do not record empty sections. `sectionSums` contains the sums in the order you record them.
2. Complete `recursiveShelvesProofStrip` so it returns `sectionSums`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [4, -5, 6, 8, 4], then `sectionSums` is [17, -1, 4, -5, 18, 6, 12, 8, 4] and `recursiveShelvesProofStrip` returns [17, -1, 4, -5, 18, 6, 12, 8, 4].

Rules
- If `sectionSums` is empty, return [].

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [0, 14, 9, 9, -6].
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [3, 3, -5, 3].

referenceSolutions.python:
def recursiveShelvesProofStrip(readings):
    a=readings
    out=[]
    def visit(left,right):
        if left>=right: return
        out.append(sum(a[left:right]))
        if right-left>1:
            mid=(left+right)//2
            visit(left,mid)
            visit(mid,right)
    visit(0,len(a))
    return out
